recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Pozole Verde with Fermented Radish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a rustic, earthy glaze, perhaps in a deep forest green or ochre tone, reflecting traditional Mexican pottery. A single generous portion of vibrant green Chicken Pozole Verde fills the bowl, showcasing whole, tender chunks of shredded chicken and plump, white hominy kernels suspended in a rich, verdant broth. The surface is subtly adorned with a scattering of freshly chopped cilantro and thin crescents of white onion, adding contrasting color and texture. A lime wedge sits on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. Alongside the bowl, on a light, reclaimed wood surface, are small, individual ceramic dishes holding vibrant pink fermented radish slices and a pinch of dried oregano. A stack of golden, crispy corn tostadas is neatly arranged beside the bowl. The setting is minimalist, with a natural undyed linen napkin and soft, diffused natural light enhancing the dish's organic colors and textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, hinting at natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with lime wedges
Dried oregano
Finely shredded fermented radish or cabbage
Tostadas or corn tortilla crisps

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (carrot ends, celery tops, onion peels, herb stems)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Radish (ahead of time): Dissolve 5g non-iodized salt in 250ml filtered water to make brine. Place thinly sliced radishes, smashed garlic (if using), and bay leaf (if using) in a clean jar. Pour brine over radishes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate.

Cook Chicken and Make Broth: Place chicken, halved onion, smashed garlic, bay leaves, 10g salt, peppercorns, and vegetable scraps in a large pot. Add 3 litres water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1-1.5 hours, or until chicken is cooked through and tender (internal temperature 75°C). Skim any foam from surface.

Shred Chicken: Remove chicken from broth. Let cool slightly. Discard bones and skin. Shred chicken meat into bite-sized pieces. Set aside. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Reserve 250ml broth for verde sauce. Keep remaining broth hot.

Prepare Verde Sauce: Roast tomatillos, poblano peppers, and jalapeños on a comal or baking sheet until softened and lightly charred. Peel poblano and jalapeño if desired. Blend roasted vegetables with roughly chopped small onion, 3 garlic cloves, roughly chopped cilantro, epazote (if using), and 250ml reserved chicken broth until smooth.

Assemble Pozole: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Pour in verde sauce. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and deepens in color. Add shredded chicken and rinsed hominy to the pot. Pour in remaining hot chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt to taste.

Serve: Ladle hot pozole into bowls. Serve with lime wedges, dried oregano, fresh chopped cilantro, thinly sliced white onion, and a side of fermented radish. Offer tostadas or corn tortilla crisps for dipping.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using chicken bones and vegetable scraps for a flavorful broth.
The fermented radish provides a tangy, probiotic element and extends the shelf life of fresh produce.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops with Coffee-Chocolate Mole and Coffee Cream
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a light, natural wooden table surface. Three perfectly seared sea scallops, displaying a beautiful golden-brown crust and tender, opaque white interiors, are artfully arranged atop a rich, glossy pool of dark coffee-chocolate mole sauce. The mole, deep brown with subtle red undertones, provides a striking contrast to the scallops. A delicate drizzle of pale, frothy coffee cream cascades over and around the scallops, adding a lighter hue and creamy texture. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are sparingly placed for a pop of color and freshness. A bright lime wedge rests beside the main arrangement, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and balanced, with ample negative space. Standard, polished flatware (fork and knife) is neatly placed beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background that suggests a modern bistro atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A small side of warm corn tortillas could be offered for dipping in the mole, though not necessary for a starter.

ingredients.name: dried ancho chili, rehydrated, deseeded, and chopped
dark chocolate (70% or higher), finely chopped

instructions: Prepare the Mole: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced white onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped ancho chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in 60 ml brewed espresso and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Stir in ground cumin, coriander, and cinnamon.
Add chopped dark chocolate. Stir until chocolate melts and sauce is smooth. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Prepare the Coffee Cream: In a small bowl, combine heavy cream, 15 ml espresso, and a pinch of salt. Whisk until slightly thickened but still pourable. Do not over-whisk.
Sear the Scallops: Pat scallops thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Place scallops in the hot skillet in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep golden-brown crust forms and scallops are cooked through.
Plate the Dish: Spoon a small pool of warm coffee-chocolate mole onto each of four white porcelain starter plates.
Arrange 3 seared scallops neatly on top of the mole on each plate.
Drizzle a small amount of coffee cream over and around the scallops.
Garnish with a few fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Corn Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A casual platter of golden-brown Chicken and Corn Fritters is arranged on a simple, well-used wooden dining table. The fritters are irregularly shaped, showcasing crispy edges and a soft, textured interior with visible pieces of finely diced chicken, bright yellow corn kernels, and specks of red chili and green coriander. They are piled naturally, not overly arranged, reflecting a homely preparation. Beside the fritters, a small ceramic bowl holds a vibrant green chili-coriander dip, flecked with red chili pieces. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comfortable, inviting atmosphere. A casually placed cloth napkin and a few stray fresh coriander leaves complete the unpretentious, family-style presentation. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, allowing for negative space around the food.
instructions: Cook chicken breast. Boil or pan-fry chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let cool. Finely dice chicken.
Prepare fritter batter. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Add wet ingredients. Whisk in egg and milk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Combine fritter ingredients. Fold in diced chicken, corn kernels, diced red onion, and chopped red chili into the batter.
Make the dip. In a small bowl, combine chopped coriander, finely chopped chili, lime juice, and Greek yogurt or sour cream. Season with salt.
Heat oil. Heat 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook fritters. Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain fritters. Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Serve hot. Serve fritters immediately with the chili-coriander dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage & Rice Bites with Fennel
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous pile of golden-brown Sausage & Rice Bites, arranged casually on a rustic wooden serving board. Each bite is irregularly shaped, showcasing a homely, unpretentious appeal. The exterior is a rich golden-brown from baking, with visible flecks of darker, cooked sausage and lighter rice. Finely diced, softened fennel and onion are subtly integrated within the bites, contributing to their textured appearance. The overall color palette is warm, with golden and reddish-brown tones from the cooked sausage and paprika. A few scattered fresh parsley leaves add a pop of vibrant green. The board is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, folded checkered cloth napkin nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen, emphasizing the comforting nature of the snack. The entire platter is visible, showcasing a casual, sharing portion suitable for relaxed eating.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Use 400 ml water. Set aside to cool.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into small pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add crumbled sausage. Cook until browned and cooked through. Break up any large pieces. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pan. Set aside.
Finely dice fennel bulb and onion. Mince garlic.
Add diced fennel and onion to the same pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, cooked sausage, sautéed fennel-onion mixture, and egg.
Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well until thoroughly combined.
Form the mixture into small, golf-ball sized bites. About 24-28 bites.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place bites on the prepared baking sheet. Ensure space between each bite.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and heated through.
Alternatively, pan-fry bites in a little oil until golden brown on all sides.
Serve warm, optionally garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta with Raspberry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta rests on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered with thoughtful negative space. The panna cotta is a smooth, creamy white cylinder, approximately 6 cm in diameter and 5 cm tall, with a delicate wobble. A vibrant, deep red raspberry coulis is artfully spooned around its base, creating an organic, flowing pool that contrasts beautifully with the panna cotta's pristine surface. A few fresh, plump raspberries are scattered beside the panna cotta, adding bursts of color and natural texture. A small, fresh mint sprig provides a subtle green accent. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its refined textures and inviting colors. The presentation is clean, professional, and balanced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served chilled, often with fresh fruit or fruit coulis. Best enjoyed as a light, sweet end to a meal.
instructions: Soak gelatin leaves in cold water for 5 minutes until softened. If using powder, sprinkle over 30 ml cold water and let bloom.
Split vanilla bean lengthwise. Scrape seeds into a medium saucepan. Add cream and sugar. Add vanilla pod.
Heat cream mixture over medium heat until simmering, stirring to dissolve sugar. Do not boil.
Remove vanilla pod. Squeeze excess water from gelatin leaves. Stir bloomed gelatin into hot cream until fully dissolved.
Pour mixture evenly into four 150 ml ramekins or molds. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For raspberry coulis, combine raspberries, 15g sugar, and lemon juice in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Pass coulis through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Chill until ready to serve.

To serve, briefly dip bottom of ramekins in hot water. Invert panna cottas onto white porcelain plates. Spoon raspberry coulis artfully around each panna cotta. Garnish with a few fresh raspberries and a small mint sprig.
notes: Ensure gelatin is fully dissolved for smooth texture. Adjust sugar in coulis to taste, depending on raspberry sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef and Mushroom Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Cooked Beef and Mushroom Ragu is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl or plate, showcasing the rich, reddish-brown sauce. Tender, shredded beef chunks are generously coated in the thick ragu, interspersed with earthy sliced cremini mushrooms and soft diced onion. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The ragu is served over a bed of golden, al dente pappardelle pasta, allowing the sauce to cling beautifully. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and deep colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh pappardelle or tagliatelle pasta, or creamy polenta.
Offer grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese for topping.
Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Trim beef chuck. Cut into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-8 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Remove pot from oven. Take beef out. Shred beef chunks using two forks. Return shredded beef to the ragu sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over fresh pasta or creamy polenta. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Classic Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The golden pappardelle pasta is coated in a rich, deep red-brown ragu, with visible, tender chunks of slow-cooked beef. A few vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the top. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese creates a light, snowy layer. Roasted broccoli florets, displaying a vibrant green hue with hints of char, are arranged neatly beside the pasta within the bowl, adding a contrasting texture and color. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a fork, a knife, and a folded cotton napkin, all under soft, natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.

Dice onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto). Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced vegetables and cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent. Mince garlic, add to pot, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low. Cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

While ragu cooks, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Once beef is tender, use two forks to shred the beef into smaller pieces within the sauce. Stir well. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and fresh basil leaves. Serve roasted broccoli alongside.
notes: For a richer flavor, allow the ragu to rest overnight in the refrigerator before reheating and serving.
The longer the ragu simmers, the more tender the beef and flavorful the sauce will be.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Pork Tenderloin with Fresh Peach and Red Onion Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of grilled pork tenderloin is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pork is cut into thick, juicy medallions with visible char marks from grilling, arranged slightly overlapping but not fanned. Beside the pork, a generous spoonful of vibrant salsa is placed, showcasing diced ripe yellow and orange peaches, finely minced red onion, and bright green chopped cilantro. The salsa provides a fresh, colorful contrast. Alongside, bright green roasted asparagus spears are neatly arranged. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard modern flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light green salad
Pair with a side of quinoa or couscous
instructions: Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill pork tenderloin for 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from heat. Rest 5 minutes.
While pork rests, prepare salsa. Dice peaches into 1 cm cubes. Finely mince half of the red onion. Roughly chop cilantro.
Combine diced peaches, minced red onion, and chopped cilantro in a bowl. Squeeze lime juice over mixture. Stir gently. Season with a pinch of salt.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss asparagus with 15 ml olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Roast asparagus for 8-10 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Slice rested pork tenderloin into thick medallions. Do not fan out.
Arrange pork medallions on serving plates. Spoon fresh peach and red onion salsa beside the pork. Place roasted asparagus alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: Use firm but ripe peaches for best texture in the salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs and Pan-Seared Chicken with Butternut Squash Puree and Tomato Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set upon a simple light wooden table. A perfectly seared, golden-brown chicken breast, skin crisp, rests beside a rich, dark brown braised beef short rib, tender and whole. Beside the meats, a vibrant, smooth orange butternut squash puree is artfully swiped across the plate. A glossy, deep reddish-brown tomato jus is generously spooned around the protein components, catching the light. Freshly chopped bright green parsley sprinkles over the meats and jus, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin to the left of the plate and a fork and knife to the right, all under natural, even lighting from the side, creating a modern bistro atmosphere with a soft, inviting glow.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs. Set aside.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into 1 cm pieces. Add to Dutch oven. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince 4 garlic cloves. Add to vegetables. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return short ribs to Dutch oven. Add beef stock, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover Dutch oven. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove short ribs from Dutch oven. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids. Skim fat from liquid.
Return liquid to heat. Reduce by half to create the tomato jus. Season to taste.
Peel and dice butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast squash on a baking sheet at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Mince remaining 4 garlic cloves. Melt 20 g butter in a small saucepan. Add garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Transfer roasted squash to a food processor. Add garlic butter. Process until smooth puree forms. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15 g butter and 15 ml olive oil.
Place chicken skin-side down in skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes.
To plate, spoon butternut squash puree onto each plate. Place a braised short rib alongside. Add a pan-seared chicken breast.
Spoon tomato jus generously over and around the meats. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The short ribs can be braised ahead of time and reheated gently in the jus.

recipes.recipe_name: Linguine with Artichokes and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: Linguine is loosely twirled onto a clean, round white porcelain plate, forming a generous, elegant mound. Tender, pale green artichoke heart halves and vibrant, julienned sun-dried tomatoes are artfully nestled within and around the pasta, creating pops of color and texture. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish, adding a subtle white contrast. Bright green, roughly chopped fresh parsley is scattered generously over the top for a final flourish. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its rich textures and inviting colors. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a modern, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Jarred artichoke hearts in brine, drained and halved
Sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and julienned

instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add halved artichoke hearts and julienned sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in vegetable broth and lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add cooked and drained linguine to the skillet. Toss to combine with the sauce.
Gradually add reserved pasta water, 60 ml at a time, while tossing until a light sauce forms and coats the pasta. The sauce should be glossy, not watery.
Stir in lemon zest and half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Remove from heat. Add half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Toss until melted and well combined.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Pork Shogayaki
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain dinner plate holds a generous portion of golden-brown, seared pork medallions, cooked as whole pieces, not fanned. Alongside the pork, glistening, tender, caramelized onion slices are nestled. A vibrant mound of finely shredded green cabbage provides a fresh counterpoint. The dish is lightly coated in a rich, glossy, savory-sweet ginger-soy glaze. Bright green, thinly sliced spring onion is scattered over the pork as a garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table. A white rice bowl and a pair of chopsticks are placed beside the dish, enhancing the authentic Japanese bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimalist and unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Serve with a side of shredded green cabbage
Can be accompanied by miso soup
Eaten with chopsticks

ingredients.name: Pork loin or shoulder, thinly sliced

instructions: Combine grated ginger, soy sauce, mirin, and sake in a small bowl. Whisk to combine. Set aside.
Slice onions into thin half-moon shapes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.

Add pork slices to the hot skillet in a single layer. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove cooked pork from skillet and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the same skillet. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Return cooked pork to the skillet with the onions.
Pour the prepared sauce over the pork and onions. Toss to coat evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the ingredients.
Serve immediately over steamed white rice, accompanied by shredded green cabbage.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Steamed Pork and Shrimp Cake
recipes.special_requests: chinese cuisine, minced pork and cut up shrimp mixed and seasoned with chinese ingredients, no garlic or onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Steamed Pork and Shrimp Cake rests in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, its off-white interior subtly contrasting the dish. The cake, a modest, round patty about 2.5 cm thick, displays a tender, slightly irregular surface, indicating its handmade nature. Its color is a natural, inviting blend of light pink from the chopped shrimp and pale brown from the minced pork, with visible flecks of both ingredients and grated ginger. The cake is moist and glistening, pooling a small amount of savory cooking liquid at its base. A few fresh, vibrant green coriander leaves are casually placed on top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside it, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a simple ceramic chopstick rest. A small bowl of fluffy white steamed rice is positioned nearby. The scene is illuminated by soft, warm kitchen light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain steamed white rice.
Offer a side of blanched green vegetables like bok choy or gai lan.
Serve with a simple, clear broth.
instructions: Peel and devein shrimp. Roughly chop the shrimp into 0.5 cm pieces.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the minced pork, chopped shrimp, grated ginger, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, cornstarch, white pepper, sugar, water, and salt.
Mix vigorously for 5 minutes. Use your hands or a spoon to combine until the mixture becomes sticky and cohesive.
Transfer the mixture to a shallow, heatproof dish suitable for steaming. Flatten the mixture evenly into a cake, about 2.5 cm thick.
Prepare a steamer. Bring water to a rolling boil in the steamer pot.
Carefully place the dish with the pork and shrimp cake into the hot steamer. Cover tightly.
Steam over high heat for 15-20 minutes. The cake is cooked when it is firm to the touch and the internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Carefully remove the dish from the steamer.
Garnish the steamed cake with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot with plain steamed white rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Caramelized Onion Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef steak is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The beef, either as a whole seared piece or thick-cut chunks, exhibits a dark, crusty sear on its exterior, contrasting with a tender, reddish-pink interior visible on any cut surfaces. A generous pool of rich, glossy caramelized onion jus surrounds the beef, with soft, deep amber-brown onion slices visibly suspended within the thickened sauce. The jus glistens under natural light, highlighting its luxurious texture. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley or chives provides a pop of green against the deep tones of the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by elegant silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, creating a sophisticated yet approachable bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Pat beef steaks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Slice onions thinly. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear steaks 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Adjust time for thickness.
Remove steaks from pan. Tent with foil. Let rest 5-10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the same pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom. Simmer 2 minutes, reducing wine slightly.
Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until sauce thickens to a jus consistency, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate beef. Spoon caramelized onion jus over and around the beef. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Steamed Pork and Shrimp Patty
recipes.special_requests: chinese cuisine, minced pork and cut up shrimp mixed and seasoned with chinese ingredients, no garlic or onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Steamed Pork and Shrimp Patty rests on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The patty, about 2.5 cm thick, is round, showcasing the tender, light brown minced pork speckled with vibrant pink roughly chopped shrimp and tiny white diced water chestnuts. A light sheen of savory cooking liquid pools around the base. It is generously garnished with bright green, thinly sliced spring onion. Beside the patty, a small mound of fluffy white steamed rice sits in a traditional Chinese rice bowl. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks lies casually across the plate's rim. The scene is set on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer a small dish of light soy sauce for dipping.

ingredients.name: Shrimp, peeled and deveined, roughly chopped

instructions: Combine minced pork, chopped shrimp, diced water chestnuts, grated ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, white pepper, and cornstarch in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly until well combined and slightly sticky.
Add 30ml water. Mix until absorbed.
Transfer mixture to a shallow, heatproof dish. Flatten into an even patty, about 2-3 cm thick.
Prepare a steamer. Bring water to a rolling boil.
Place dish in steamer. Steam for 15-20 minutes.
Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from steamer. Garnish with sliced spring onion.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Caramelized Onions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A large, rustic chunk of dark brown, fork-tender braised beef, its surface glistening, is positioned slightly off-center. Beneath and around the beef is a generous bed of deeply caramelized, soft, golden-brown onion slices, showing their rich, glossy texture. A dark, glossy, rich pan sauce is artfully spooned over the beef and pooled around the base, creating a sheen. A small sprig of fresh thyme rests gently on top of the beef, adding a touch of green. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Add a pinch of sugar if needed to aid caramelization.
Add chopped carrots, celery, and minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Pour in beef broth. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef chunks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid. Cover the pot with a lid.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Carefully remove beef from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.

Skim any excess fat from the strained liquid. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until the sauce slightly thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Stir in butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve each beef chunk with a generous portion of the caramelized onions and a ladle of the rich pan sauce.
notes: For best flavor, braise the beef a day in advance. Cool completely, then refrigerate. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the oven.
Adjust the consistency of the sauce by reducing it further for a thicker glaze or adding a splash of broth for a thinner consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Stir-fried Pork and Shrimp with Green Beans
recipes.special_requests: chinese cuisine, minced pork and cut up shrimp mixed and seasoned with chinese ingredients
recipes.visual_description: A modest, homely single portion of Homestyle Stir-fried Pork and Shrimp with Green Beans is presented on a simple, light-colored ceramic plate. To one side, a neat mound of fluffy white rice sits, ready to accompany the main dish. The stir-fry is casually spooned next to the rice, creating an inviting, natural arrangement. Minced pork, browned and savory, is mixed with tender, pinkish-orange diced shrimp. Vibrant green, crisp-tender green bean pieces, cut into 2-3 cm lengths, are interspersed throughout, adding a pop of color and texture. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, rich brown sauce, reflecting the warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures. The textures are varied: the tender pork, the firm shrimp, and the slight bite of the green beans. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple ceramic rice bowl and a pair of traditional chopsticks nearby. A casually placed cloth napkin completes the lived-in, family kitchen atmosphere, with minimal background elements to keep the focus on the comforting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with hot steamed white rice.
Can be accompanied by a simple clear soup or a light vegetable dish.
instructions: Cut green beans into 2-3 cm pieces. Dice peeled shrimp into small pieces.
In a bowl, combine minced pork with 5 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml Shaoxing wine, 1.25 ml white pepper, and 5 g cornstarch. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine diced shrimp with 5 ml Shaoxing wine, 1.25 ml white pepper, and 5 g cornstarch. Mix well.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add green beans. Blanch for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat until shimmering.
Add minced pork. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, breaking it apart, until browned and cooked through. Remove pork from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced shrimp to the wok. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until pink and nearly cooked. Do not overcook.
Return cooked pork and blanched green beans to the wok.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 20 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml dark soy sauce, 15 ml oyster sauce, and 60 ml water or chicken stock. Pour sauce over ingredients in the wok.
Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, tossing to coat everything evenly. Sauce will thicken slightly.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Toss briefly. Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
notes: Ensure wok is very hot before adding ingredients for proper stir-frying.
Do not overcook shrimp; they cook very quickly.
The green beans are blanched first to ensure even cooking and vibrant color.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken and Bean Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A collection of golden-brown Savory Chicken and Bean Fritters are casually arranged on a rustic, off-white ceramic sharing platter. The fritters are irregularly shaped, showcasing slightly crispy, uneven edges and a hearty, homely appearance. Some fritters are stacked loosely, others are scattered around the platter, indicating a relaxed, family-style serving. The interior of a few fritters, where visible, reveals a comforting mix of light shredded chicken, soft white rice grains, and dark, slightly mashed black beans, flecked with finely diced onion. The natural colors are warm and inviting, ranging from the deep golden exterior to the varied textures within. The platter rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting. A casually folded, plain cloth napkin sits nearby. The background is minimal, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, highlighting the unpretentious, comforting nature of the snack. Portions are generous, inviting sharing.
instructions: Shred cooked chicken breast into small pieces. Ensure no large chunks.
Finely dice the onion. Sauté in a pan with a small amount of oil until softened and translucent. Let cool.
In a large bowl, lightly mash the cooked black beans with a fork. Leave some texture.
Add shredded chicken, cooked rice, sautéed onion, egg, flour, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to the bowl with the beans.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly until well combined. The mixture should hold together.
Form the mixture into 12-16 small, flat fritters, about 5-6 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place fritters in the hot pan, do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Fry for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot Risotto with Toasted Walnuts and Goat Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of vibrant fuchsia-hued risotto, creamy and fluid, is artfully mounded on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto maintains a soft, natural flow, avoiding any rigid or molded shapes. Scattered over the surface are rough-chopped, golden-brown toasted walnuts, adding textural contrast. Crumbled white goat cheese pieces are nestled amidst the risotto, creating soft color variation. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped chives provides a fresh, aromatic finish. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the risotto's rich color and texture to dominate. The beets are pureed for color and diced into small cubes for texture. Walnuts are roughly chopped. Chives are finely chopped. Goat cheese is crumbled. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro. A neatly folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its rich color and creamy sheen. The background is subtly blurred, featuring a hint of a casual restaurant atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Pair with a light side salad or crusty bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and trim beets. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes until tender. Let cool slightly.
Peel beets. Puree half the roasted beets with a splash of water until smooth. Dice the remaining half into small cubes. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced shallots. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add the beet puree to the rice. Stir until well combined and heated through.
Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Allow each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and the rice al dente.
Stir in the diced beets. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano. If using butter, add remaining 15 g butter. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. This is 'mantecatura'.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. The risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Meanwhile, toast walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Roughly chop.
Serve risotto immediately in warm bowls or plates. Garnish each serving with crumbled goat cheese, toasted walnuts, and finely chopped chives.
notes: The key to creamy risotto is constant stirring and gradual addition of hot broth. Adjust broth quantity for desired consistency.
For a vegan option, substitute butter with olive oil and use a plant-based parmesan alternative and vegan 'goat' cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili-Sesame Fermented Bell Pepper Salad
recipes.visual_description: A small, individual starter portion of vibrant fermented bell pepper and red onion salad. Diced red, yellow, and orange bell peppers are mixed with thinly sliced red onion. The vegetables retain a crisp-tender texture, glistening lightly with a chili-sesame dressing. A few very thin rounds of red chili are scattered on top. The salad is mounded artfully in the center of a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving generous negative space. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is subtly placed beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, clean colors and natural textures of the ingredients. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Wash bell peppers and onion. Remove bell pepper cores.
Dice all bell peppers into 1cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion.
Combine diced bell peppers and sliced onion in a clean 1.5-liter glass jar.
Dissolve salt in non-chlorinated water to create a brine. Pour brine over vegetables in the jar. Ensure all vegetables are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover jar loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp jar daily if not using an airlock.
Once fermented, drain vegetables. Discard brine or reserve for other uses.
Thinly slice red chili into rounds.
In a bowl, combine fermented vegetables, brown rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, and sliced chili. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately as a starter.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Sticky Rice with Mango
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coconut Sticky Rice with Mango is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous, glossy scoop of creamy, pale ivory sticky rice is placed on one side of the plate. Beside it, bright yellow-orange mango flesh, cut into thick, uniform batons, is arranged in a slight curve. The vibrant colors contrast beautifully. A sprinkle of bright green lime zest is scattered over the mango and rice, alongside a few golden toasted coconut flakes, adding textural contrast. The dish is illuminated by natural, even lighting. The background features a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin, creating a clean, inviting, and authentic Thai dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon.
Often served as a dessert or a sweet snack.
instructions: Rinse glutinous rice several times until water runs clear. Soak rice in cold water for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Drain soaked rice completely. Place rice in a steamer basket lined with cheesecloth. Steam rice over boiling water for 20-25 minutes, until tender and translucent.
While rice steams, combine coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a saucepan. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.

Once rice is cooked, transfer it to a large bowl. Pour warm coconut milk mixture over the rice. Stir gently to combine. Cover the bowl and let it sit for 15-20 minutes, allowing the rice to absorb the liquid.
Peel mangoes. Slice mango flesh into thick, even batons or wedges.
Zest the lime.
To serve, scoop warm sticky rice onto individual plates. Arrange mango slices neatly beside the rice. Garnish with fresh lime zest and toasted coconut flakes, if using.
notes: Adjust sugar to your preference based on mango sweetness.
Ensure rice is thoroughly drained before steaming for best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Braised Pork Belly with Pan-Seared Prawns
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of an ultra-sophisticated Chinese main course is presented on an off-white, modern designer bone china plate. The plate rests on a subtly veined grey marble surface. Two thick, glistening cubes of red-braised pork belly are artfully arranged slightly off-center, their dark mahogany glaze catching the dramatic overhead light. Alongside, two perfectly pan-seared jumbo prawns, tails intact, display vibrant orange and pink hues. A single, small, vibrant green bok choy head is meticulously placed for subtle color contrast. A delicate drizzle of the reduced, glossy braising sauce cascades elegantly around the pork. The dish is garnished precisely with a small, neat pile of finely julienned fresh ginger and thinly sliced green spring onion rounds. Abundant negative space emphasizes minimalist elegance. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, and elegant wooden chopsticks complete the authentic cultural setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of blanched gai lan.

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, skin on, cut into 4 cm thick chunks

ingredients.name: Spring Onions
ingredients.quantity: 3 stalks, 2 stalks cut into 5 cm lengths, 1 stalk thinly sliced for garnish

instructions: Blanch pork belly chunks in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse thoroughly.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a wok or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add sliced ginger and 5 cm spring onion lengths. Sauté until fragrant.
Add blanched pork belly. Sear until lightly browned on all sides.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, star anise, and cinnamon stick. Stir well.
Pour in 500 ml water, or enough to just cover the pork. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is very tender. Turn pork occasionally.
Remove pork from braising liquid. Strain braising liquid into a clean saucepan. Discard aromatics.
Return pork to the strained braising liquid. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 15-20 minutes, reducing sauce until it coats the pork.
Season prawns with salt and white pepper. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear prawns for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and cooked through.
Blanch bok choy in boiling salted water for 1 minute. Drain.
notes: Blanching pork belly removes impurities, ensuring cleaner flavor.
Adjust rock sugar to desired sweetness.
The braising liquid should reduce to a thick, glossy sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato Skin Crisps with Spicy Veggie Relish
recipes.visual_description: The snack is presented on a minimalist, unglazed natural ceramic plate in a soft cream hue, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. Four halved, crisp potato skins are arranged with clean spacing, highlighting their golden-brown, slightly blistered texture. Each skin is generously filled with a creamy, pale yellow fermented potato mash, showing subtle air pockets from fermentation. This base is topped with a vibrant, finely diced relish. The relish features small, distinct cubes of bright red bell pepper, vibrant green beans, and red tomato, interspersed with translucent pieces of fermented onion. The natural colors and textures of the vegetables are prominent. The overall composition is clean, organic, and unfussy, emphasizing the natural beauty and textures of the ingredients. The background is simple and uncluttered, with soft, natural light illuminating the dish. The entire plate is visible.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes thoroughly. Pierce each potato several times with a fork. Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until tender.
Once cool enough to handle, halve each potato lengthwise. Carefully scoop out the cooked potato flesh, leaving a 5mm border of flesh attached to the skin. Reserve the skins.
Mash the scooped potato flesh in a bowl. Finely dice half of the small red onion. Add diced onion, 15ml hot sauce, and 3g sea salt to the mashed potato. Mix well.

Pack the potato mixture tightly into a clean 500ml jar, leaving 2cm headspace. Press down to remove air pockets. Cover loosely with a lid or fermentation airlock. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 24-48 hours, or until a pleasant tangy aroma develops.
While potato filling ferments, finely dice the red bell pepper, green beans, cherry tomatoes, and the remaining half of the red onion. Combine all diced vegetables in a clean 500ml jar.

Dissolve 7g sea salt in 200ml filtered water to create a brine. Pour brine over the diced vegetables in the jar, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if necessary to keep vegetables below the brine. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess is reached.
While fermentation occurs, brush the reserved potato skins (inside and out) with olive oil. Place them cut-side up on a baking tray. Bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.

Once fermented, refrigerate both potato filling and relish. To assemble, spoon a generous amount of fermented potato filling into each crisp potato skin. Top with a spoonful of the fermented veggie relish.
Serve immediately as a sustainable, flavorful snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Roasted Tomato and Bell Pepper Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared cod sits centrally on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The cod, a thick, flaky piece, exhibits a beautifully golden-brown, crispy crust on top, contrasting with its moist, pearly white interior. It is nestled atop a vibrant, colorful relish of roasted cherry tomatoes and diced red and yellow bell peppers. The tomatoes are plump and slightly burst, revealing their juicy interiors, while the bell peppers are tender with subtly charred edges, adding depth. Finely diced red onion and minced garlic are interspersed within the relish, which has a glossy sheen from olive oil and pan juices. Freshly chopped bright green basil and parsley are generously scattered over the relish, providing a fresh, aromatic contrast. A quarter lemon wedge, cut lengthwise, is placed beside the fish, ready to be squeezed. The plate has ample negative space, showcasing the dish's refined simplicity. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light-colored, clean wooden table surface. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate, accompanied by standard polished silver flatware. Natural, soft, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors of the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss halved cherry tomatoes, diced red and yellow bell peppers, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, pat cod fillets dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place cod fillets presentation-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Flip cod. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 63°C and fish flakes easily.
Remove cod from pan. Keep warm.
Deglaze pan with white wine (or broth), scraping up browned bits. Reduce slightly.
Add roasted vegetables to the pan. Stir to combine with pan sauce.
Stir in chopped basil and parsley. Squeeze half a lemon over the relish. Adjust seasoning.
Plate each cod fillet on a bed of the roasted tomato and bell pepper relish. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Basil Chicken and Vegetable Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and aromatic individual portion of Spicy Basil Chicken and Vegetable Noodles is presented in a clean, wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dark, glossy wide rice noodles are intertwined with an abundance of colorful, crisp-tender vegetables and succulent chicken chunks. Prominent are chunks of golden-brown stir-fried chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets, ruby-red bell pepper strips, deep purple eggplant cubes, and bright green green bean pieces. Sliced mushrooms and halved cherry tomatoes add further color and texture. The dish is generously speckled with fragrant, wilted fresh Thai basil leaves and thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies, providing a pop of green and red. The sauce glistens, coating all ingredients evenly without being soupy. There is appropriate negative space on the plate's rim. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests neatly beside the bowl, and a small, white ceramic ramekin of additional sliced chilies is placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer extra fish sauce, chili flakes, or sliced fresh chilies on the side for individual spice and seasoning adjustment.
Serve with a simple clear broth on the side.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks and a large spoon.

ingredients.name: small red bird's eye chilies, thinly sliced
medium onion, sliced into thin wedges
red bell pepper, deseeded and sliced into 1 cm strips
small Japanese eggplant, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
green beans, trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces
fresh shiitake or cremini mushrooms, sliced
fresh Thai basil leaves, roughly torn

instructions: Soak dried rice noodles in hot water for 10-15 minutes until pliable but still firm. Drain well.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water or broth. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add chicken chunks to the hot wok. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add onion, bell pepper, broccoli, eggplant, green beans, and mushrooms. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add soaked noodles and cherry tomatoes. Pour the prepared sauce over everything. Toss well to combine, ensuring noodles are coated.
Mix 5g cornstarch with 15ml water to create a slurry. Stir the slurry into the wok. Continue to toss for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and coats the noodles and ingredients.
Remove wok from heat. Stir in fresh basil leaves until just wilted.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
For best results, use a very hot wok or large skillet. Cook in batches if your pan is not large enough to avoid overcrowding, which steams rather than stir-fries.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cashew Chicken with Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Spicy Cashew Chicken with Green Beans rests casually on a round, light-colored ceramic plate. The dish features tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, cooked to a safe 75°C, nestled amongst vibrant green beans. The chicken, seared to develop a slight crust, is coated in a glossy, dark, savory-sweet sauce. Crunchy, pale cashews are scattered throughout, adding textural contrast. Thinly sliced red chilies and minced garlic are visible, providing pops of color and aromatic notes. The green beans are crisp-tender, their natural verdant hue contrasting with the sauce. The components are arranged naturally, overlapping slightly, as if served directly from the pan onto a family kitchen table. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple white rice bowl filled with steamed jasmine rice is placed beside the main dish. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests across the rice bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy natural light, suggesting a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the homely, comforting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with hot steamed jasmine rice.
Offer extra sliced chilies or chili flakes on the side for those who prefer more heat.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm bite-sized chunks. Place in a bowl.
Add 15 ml soy sauce and 5 g cornstarch to chicken. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Trim ends off green beans. Halve longer beans.
Mince garlic. Slice red chilies thinly. Grate ginger.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, remaining 10 g cornstarch, and 60 ml water or chicken broth. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add chicken in a single layer. Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to wok. Add minced garlic, sliced chilies, and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add green beans to wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to wok. Add cashews.
Stir sauce mixture again. Pour into wok. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted sesame oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of red chilies to suit your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast, Caramelized Pineapple, Daikon Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast, artfully arranged on a pristine white bone china plate. The duck, with its deeply golden, crisp skin and succulent pink interior, is sliced into thick, generous pieces, presented as whole chunks. Scattered around are glistening, caramelized pineapple cubes, their golden hue contrasting with the duck. Beside them, a delicate, airy mound of ultra-thin daikon radish rounds adds a crisp, translucent counterpoint. A few vibrant green microgreens are precisely placed for a pop of color and freshness. The composition is elegantly minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate rests on a dark, polished wooden table, illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting, casting soft shadows. A perfectly folded white linen napkin is positioned nearby, completing the luxurious setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into the flesh.
Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in a cold, oven-safe pan.
Render duck fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes. Skin should be golden and crisp.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 60°C.
Remove duck from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes.
While duck rests, cut pineapple into 1.5 cm cubes.
In a clean pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add pineapple cubes and sugar.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until pineapple is caramelized and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Peel daikon radish. Use a mandoline to slice daikon into very thin rounds.
In a small bowl, combine rice vinegar, olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Gently dress daikon slices.
Slice each rested duck breast into 2-3 thick pieces.
Arrange duck pieces off-center on each plate. Do not fan slices.
Artfully scatter caramelized pineapple cubes around the duck.
Neatly arrange a small, delicate pile of daikon radish slices beside the duck.
Garnish with microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Beef and Chorizo Stew with Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Beef and Chorizo Stew is presented on a clean, white round porcelain dinner plate, centered elegantly. On one side, a generous mound of vibrant golden saffron rice, fluffy and distinct, is carefully placed. Adjacent to it, the rich, deep reddish-brown stew with tender, succulent chunks of braised beef and thick slices of reddish-orange chorizo is spooned. Scattered within the stew are softened pieces of red and green bell peppers, along with bright yellow corn kernels, adding pops of color. The stew's sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adorns both the stew and the rice, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, dark wooden table surface with a natural texture. A clean white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is bathed in soft, even natural light, highlighting the food's texture and color. Traditional Spanish flatware (fork and knife) is placed appropriately.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the stew's rich sauce
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and sherry vinegar on the side
Pair with a robust Spanish red wine
instructions: Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Slice chorizo into 1 cm thick rounds. Add to the same pot and cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo and set aside.
Chop onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in 50 ml chicken stock to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Return beef to the pot.
Pour in remaining 700 ml chicken stock, ensuring beef is mostly submerged. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
In the last 30 minutes of braising, add the cooked chorizo and corn kernels to the stew. Continue simmering uncovered to slightly reduce the sauce.

While stew braises, prepare saffron rice. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a separate pot. Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes. In a small bowl, steep saffron threads in 250 ml hot chicken stock or water for 5 minutes. Add saffron liquid to the rice. Cook according to rice package directions until tender and liquid is absorbed.
Taste stew and adjust seasoning. Remove bay leaf.
Serve generous portions of the braised beef and chorizo stew alongside a mound of saffron rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, braise the stew a day ahead; flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust spice level of chorizo based on preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Chili-Garlic & Crispy Bean Cakes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked chicken and crispy bean cakes is presented on a natural, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone like cream or beige. The boneless chicken thigh, moist and tender, rests centrally, displaying its natural shape and a subtle golden-brown sear. Alongside it, two round, golden-crisp bean cakes, approximately 6cm in diameter, are neatly placed. A rich, deep reddish-brown sauce, derived from the fermented chili-garlic paste, is artfully spooned around the main components, creating a natural flow. The dish is garnished with a scattering of roughly chopped toasted cashews for texture and a few fresh, vibrant green flat-leaf parsley or cilantro leaves for a pop of color. A light dusting of fine lemon zest adds subtle brightness. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing each ingredient's natural beauty to shine. The plate sits on a light bamboo table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, and a clean, minimalist background with a subtle green plant enhances the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Chili-Garlic Paste: Finely chop red chilies and garlic cloves. Combine them in a clean jar. Mix white wine vinegar, water, and sugar to create a brine. Pour brine over chilies and garlic, ensuring they are submerged. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once fermented.

Prepare Chicken: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Sear chicken in 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan until golden brown on both sides. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make Bean Cakes: Drain cooked white beans, reserving 100ml liquid. Mash beans coarsely. Mix mashed beans with cornstarch, reserved bean liquid, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Form into 8 round patties, approximately 6cm diameter and 1.5cm thick.
Cook Bean Cakes: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pan-fry bean cakes for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Prepare Cashew Crumble: Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden. Roughly chop toasted cashews.
Finish Sauce: Once chicken is cooked, remove from pan. Deglaze pan with 30ml of the fermented chili-garlic paste, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer briefly to thicken slightly.

Plate Dish: Place one slow-cooked chicken thigh on each handcrafted ceramic plate. Arrange two crispy bean cakes alongside the chicken. Spoon the warm chili-garlic sauce generously over and around the chicken and bean cakes. Garnish with scattered toasted cashew crumble, fresh parsley or cilantro leaves, and finely grated lemon zest. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Tuna with Asian Chickpea-Cucumber Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A thick, pan-seared tuna steak anchors the clean white porcelain plate, presenting a beautiful golden-brown crust with a visible pink-red interior from a perfect medium-rare cook. The tuna is presented as a whole, unsliced chunk. Adjacent to the tuna, a vibrant mound of Asian chickpea-cucumber salsa creates a striking color contrast. The salsa features small-diced green cucumber, pale yellow chickpeas, and finely diced purple-red onion, all glistening lightly from the dressing. Fresh green cilantro sprigs or thinly sliced green onions are scattered over the salsa for a pop of freshness. The plate sits on a simple dark wooden table, accompanied by a set of clean chopsticks and a small ceramic soy dish, creating a modern bistro setting with an authentic Asian touch. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of extra soy sauce or a light ponzu for dipping.

ingredients.name: Fresh cilantro or green onions, chopped

instructions: Prepare the salsa: In a medium bowl, combine the drained chickpeas, small-diced cucumber, and finely diced red onion.
Make the dressing: In a separate small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and honey/sugar.
Pour the dressing over the salsa mixture. Stir gently to combine. Set aside to marinate for at least 10 minutes.
Season tuna steaks generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick or cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place tuna steaks in the hot skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness. The exterior should be golden-brown.
Remove tuna from skillet. Let rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Place one seared tuna steak on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the chickpea-cucumber salsa alongside the tuna. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Chicken with Braised White Beans & Cashew Cream
recipes.visual_description: A handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone holds a single, refined portion. Tender, braised white beans form a natural base. A perfectly seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp, rests whole atop the beans. Velvety, off-white cashew cream is artfully drizzled over the chicken and beans, creating soft, flowing lines. Vibrant, deep red fermented chili paste is applied in delicate dollops, adding a pop of color. The composition is clean, with ample white space, emphasizing each ingredient's natural beauty. Subtle garnishes include a few delicate green herb leaves and a thin slice of red chili. The setting features a light bamboo surface, undyed linen napkin, and soft natural light, enhancing the dish's organic appeal.

ingredients.name: Dried white beans (cannellini or butter beans)
Light lager or pale ale beer
Fresh herbs (e.g., parsley or cilantro leaves)

instructions: Soak white beans in cold water overnight. Drain and rinse.
In a large pot, combine drained beans, finely diced onion/shallot, 2 minced garlic cloves, beer, and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cook beans over low heat for 60-90 minutes, or until tender. Season with salt and pepper.
For cashew cream: Soak cashews in hot water for 30 minutes. Drain. Blend soaked cashews with 120ml fresh water and a pinch of salt until very smooth and creamy. Adjust water for desired consistency.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes.
To plate: Spoon a generous portion of braised white beans onto the center of each plate.
Place one seared chicken thigh on top of the beans.
Drizzle cashew cream artfully over the chicken and beans.
Add small dollops or a thin drizzle of fermented chili paste. Optionally, add a dash of hot sauce for extra heat.
Garnish minimally with thinly sliced fresh chili and a few herb leaves, if desired.
notes: Emphasizes fermentation for flavor depth and preservation.
Zero-waste approach includes using vegetable scraps for broth and minimizing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper and Anchovy Linguine
recipes.visual_description: Roasted Bell Pepper and Anchovy Linguine is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant interplay of colors and textures. The golden linguine is lightly coated in a glossy, emulsified sauce infused with dissolved anchovy and garlic. Interspersed throughout are tender, char-kissed strips of roasted red and yellow bell peppers, adding sweet notes and visual depth. Fresh green onion slices are sprinkled generously over the top, providing a crisp green contrast and aromatic freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese adds a subtle white accent. The dish is arranged with a natural, flowing elegance, allowing the individual components to be clearly seen without being overcrowded. Moderate negative space frames the central portion, inviting appreciation of each element. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting from above. A folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware rest beside the bowl, completing the approachable bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine, such as a Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into 1.5 cm wide strips. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add linguine and cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, thinly slice green onions, separating white and green parts. Mince garlic.
Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add anchovy fillets. Cook, stirring, until anchovies dissolve into a paste, about 2-3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add the white parts of the green onions to the skillet. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Drain pasta, reserving 250 ml of pasta water. Add pasta directly to the skillet with the anchovy mixture. Add roasted bell peppers.
Add 125 ml of reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to combine. The sauce should emulsify and coat the pasta. Add more pasta water, 30 ml at a time, if needed for desired consistency.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley and the green parts of the green onions. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately with grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: The anchovies dissolve completely, leaving behind a rich, savory umami flavor, not a 'fishy' taste.
Adjust red pepper flakes to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Emulsifying pasta sauce with pasta water

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Thyme Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is positioned as the focal point. Rustic chunks of tender, braised potatoes, some with subtly browned edges, are arranged around the chicken. Soft, caramelized onion pieces are nestled among the potatoes and chicken. A rich, glossy, reduced pan sauce pools elegantly around the ingredients, adding depth and moisture. The color palette features the deep amber of the chicken skin, pale yellow potatoes, and the savory brown of the sauce, accented by fresh green thyme sprigs. The composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing refined rustic appeal. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate on a simple wooden table surface under natural, even lighting. This is a single, refined restaurant-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the savory sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a good accompaniment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up.
Add potato chunks around the chicken. Ensure potatoes are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid. Increase oven temperature to 200°C (400°F) for 10-15 minutes to crisp chicken skin, if desired.
Rest chicken briefly before serving.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs adds more flavor and helps keep the chicken moist during braising.
Adjust the amount of chicken stock to ensure potatoes are partially submerged but not swimming. The sauce should be rich, not watery.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Beer-Braised Chicken with Quick-Pickled Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Beer-Braised Chicken is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving generous negative space. A bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and crisped, rests as the central focus. Beneath it, a rich, dark brown braising liquid pools naturally. To one side, a small, artful mound of quick-pickled black beans, glossy and dark, with visible slivers of bright red chili and minced garlic, adds a contrasting texture and color. A generous, organic swirl of creamy white cashew sauce is drizzled across the chicken and beans. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves. The entire plate is visible, placed on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's earthy color palette and organic forms, with a clean, minimalist background that hints at natural elements.

ingredients.name: Dried red chilies (e.g., arbol), deseeded and chopped

instructions: Soak black beans overnight. Drain.
Boil soaked beans until tender, about 45-60 minutes. Drain. Let cool slightly.
For quick-pickled beans: In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, 125ml water, 5g salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer until salt and sugar dissolve. Let cool.
