Combine cooked beans with 1 minced garlic clove and 1 chopped dried chili. Pour cooled pickling liquid over beans. Stir. Set aside to quick-pickle for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for longer preservation.
For cashew cream: Soak cashews in hot water for 30 minutes. Drain. Blend cashews with 125ml fresh water and a pinch of salt until completely smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until skin is deeply golden and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Pour off excess fat, leaving about 15ml.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add remaining minced garlic and chopped chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and hot sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. If not, add a little more stock or water.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce braising liquid until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes.
Serve each chicken thigh with a ladle of reduced braising liquid. Add a generous spoonful of quick-pickled beans alongside. Drizzle with cashew cream. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using bone-in chicken (bones can be used for stock) and quick-pickling beans for preservation. Save vegetable scraps for future stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Orzo Salad with Lemon-Herb Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: Broccoli and Orzo Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of textures and colors. Small, tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets, some with subtle charred edges, are interspersed with tiny, rice-shaped orzo pasta. Creamy white mozzarella, cut into 1cm cubes, provides soft contrast. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes and thinly sliced crimson red onion add bursts of color. The salad is gently tossed, allowing the ingredients to mingle naturally, coated in a glistening lemon vinaigrette. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley and golden pine nuts provides a fresh garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, evoking a relaxed modern bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread or focaccia.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Toss with 15ml olive oil, 2g salt, 1g black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Let cool.
Cook orzo pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to cool quickly. Drain thoroughly again.
If using larger mozzarella, cut into 1cm cubes. In a small bowl, combine mozzarella with 5ml olive oil, 2g dried oregano, and zest of half a lemon. Toss gently.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice or finely dice red onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 40ml olive oil, juice of one lemon, minced garlic, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
In a large serving bowl, combine cooled orzo, roasted broccoli, marinated mozzarella, halved cherry tomatoes, and diced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish salad with fresh parsley and pine nuts (if using). Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Chicken with Pickled Radish & Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Fermented Chili Chicken with Pickled Radish & Rice is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl, in a natural cream or beige tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A generous bed of fluffy brown rice forms the base, its earthy hue providing a natural contrast. Beside it, two to three rustic, thick chunks of seared chicken thigh, with a visibly crispy, golden-brown skin, are neatly placed. The rich, deep red-orange of the chili marinade is subtly visible on the chicken. Bright, thinly sliced pickled radishes and cucumber half-moons, vibrant pink and green respectively, are arranged alongside, adding pops of color and a fresh, crisp texture. A few fresh cilantro or mint leaves are thoughtfully placed as a natural, unfussy garnish, providing a hint of vibrant green. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing each ingredient’s natural beauty and texture to stand out. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle hints of natural elements like a blurred potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. The entire bowl is visible, with ample white space around it.

ingredients.name: Red chilies (e.g., Fresno or bird's eye), chopped
Fresh cilantro or mint, for garnish

instructions: Prepare fermented chili paste: Combine chopped chilies, garlic, ginger, salt, and water in a blender. Blend until smooth. Transfer to a clean, air-tight jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate.
Marinate chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, coat chicken with 30g of the fermented chili paste. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.

Prepare quick pickles: In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, sugar, and 50ml water. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Let cool completely. Place sliced radishes and cucumber in a clean jar. Pour cooled pickling liquid over vegetables. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Cook rice: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cook chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Heat cooking oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes. Cut chicken into thick, rustic chunks.

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among four serving bowls. Arrange chicken chunks on one side of the rice. Drain pickled radishes and cucumber. Arrange pickled vegetables beside the chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro or mint leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Rice Stuffed Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: One plump, ruby-red Beef and Rice Stuffed Tomato sits centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tomato is whole, its top sliced off and set slightly askew, revealing the rich, savory filling within. The filling consists of finely diced beef, fluffy white rice, vibrant red tomato pieces, and aromatic herbs, all gently mounded inside the tomato cavity. A golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella cheese covers the top, with hints of fresh green parsley sprigs scattered over. The tomato itself is tender, slightly collapsed from baking, but retaining its shape. The plate has ample negative space. A simple wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin, and modern flatware accompany the dish. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting warmth and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the tomato juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a baking dish.
Wash tomatoes. Slice off the top 1 cm from each tomato. Scoop out the pulp and seeds. Reserve the pulp. Invert tomato shells on paper towels to drain.
Chop the reserved tomato pulp finely.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the pan. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned, ensuring no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato pulp and beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing liquid to reduce slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in cooked rice, chopped parsley, and chopped basil. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Mix well.
Spoon the beef and rice mixture into each hollowed tomato shell. Do not overfill.
Place stuffed tomatoes in the prepared baking dish. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese generously over each tomato.
Return to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and golden brown and internal temperature of beef is 75°C.
notes: Choose firm, ripe tomatoes that can hold their shape during baking.
Any leftover filling can be served as a side dish or frozen for later use.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Herbed White Bean Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, golden-brown with a lightly crisp exterior, rests centrally on a creamy, rich white bean ragout. The chicken is presented as a whole, substantial piece. The ragout is a loose, slightly chunky blend of tender cannellini beans, halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes, and finely minced shallots and garlic, infused with fresh thyme. Thinly sliced bright green green onions and a few fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a fresh, verdant contrast. The dish is served on a clean, round white porcelain plate, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the delicious ragout.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and minced shallots to the skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.

Add rinsed cannellini beans, halved cherry tomatoes, and thyme sprigs to the skillet. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften slightly and sauce thickens. Season the ragout with salt and pepper.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet with the ragout. Spoon some ragout over the chicken. Cook for 1-2 minutes to reheat.
Serve chicken thighs immediately over the herbed white bean ragout. Garnish each portion with thinly sliced green onions and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger Pork and Shiitake with Dashi Glaze
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Three to four thick, pan-seared pork medallions, exhibiting a rich golden-brown crust, are arranged centrally. Each pork chunk is coated in a glossy, amber-brown dashi-ginger glaze. Sautéed shiitake mushroom slices, also gleaming with glaze, are scattered alongside, adding earthy tones. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced green onions for vibrant color. Moderate negative space is maintained on the plate. A small, elegant white ceramic bowl of perfectly steamed white rice accompanies the main plate. Traditional wooden chopsticks rest beside the rice bowl. The setting is a simple wooden table surface with natural, even lighting and a subtle modern bistro background, showcasing an authentic Japanese culinary aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white rice.
Offer a small dish of pickled ginger or daikon as a palate cleanser.
Use traditional Japanese bowls for rice and a shallow plate for the main dish.
instructions: Pat pork medallions dry. Season lightly with salt and black pepper.
Prepare dashi glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, and dashi stock.
In another small bowl, dissolve cornstarch in cold water to make a slurry. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add pork medallions to the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove pork from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the same pan. Add sliced shiitake mushrooms. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add grated ginger to the pan with shiitake. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour dashi glaze mixture into the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in cornstarch slurry gradually until sauce thickens to a glossy consistency.
Return seared pork medallions to the pan. Turn to coat pork and shiitake thoroughly with the glaze. Cook for 1-2 minutes until heated through.
Stir in sesame oil.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust ginger quantity to personal preference for more or less pungency.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Ricotta Gnudi with Brown Butter and Sage
recipes.visual_description: A small starter portion of delicate, pillowy Spinach and Ricotta Gnudi, artfully arranged on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Each gnudi, roughly 4cm in diameter and irregularly shaped, boasts a pale green hue from the finely chopped spinach, contrasting with creamy white interior peeking through. They are lightly coated in a shimmering, nutty brown butter sauce, which collects subtly at the base. Fresh, vibrant green sage leaves, some whole and some lightly fried to a crisp, are scattered elegantly over and around the gnudi. The composition is organic, with moderate negative space, showcasing the gnudi as the focal point. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere suitable for a casual bistro setting. A folded white linen napkin is placed beside the plate. The presentation is clean, professional, and highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
Offer fresh, crusty bread for dipping in the leftover brown butter sauce.

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour, plus more for dusting

instructions: Wash spinach thoroughly. Blanch spinach in boiling salted water for 1 minute. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Squeeze out all excess water very thoroughly. Finely chop the spinach.
Place ricotta and cottage cheese in a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Let drain over a bowl in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, to remove excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine drained ricotta, cottage cheese, chopped spinach, grated Parmesan, egg, flour, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.

Lightly flour a clean work surface. Scoop small portions of the mixture, about 20-25 grams each. Gently roll each portion into an irregular, roughly 4cm oval or dumpling shape. Dust lightly with flour. Arrange gnudi on a floured baking sheet.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully drop gnudi into the simmering water in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Cook gnudi for 3-4 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon. Place on a warm plate.
While gnudi cook, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Add sage leaves. Cook until sage is crisp. Remove from heat.
Divide cooked gnudi among four starter plates. Drizzle generously with brown butter and crisp sage leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, tender chicken thigh rests centrally, generously coated and surrounded by a rich, deep red tomato-garlic sauce. The rustic, slightly chunky sauce features diced red bell pepper and minced garlic. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley garnishes the dish. Plating is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. Traditional Spanish crusty bread, cut into thick chunks, is in a small rustic bowl nearby, perfect for dipping. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (Pan de Pueblo) to soak up the sauce
Serve alongside a simple rice pilaf or roasted potatoes
Pair with a dry Spanish red wine like Rioja or Tempranillo
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced red bell pepper, and sliced fresh chili (if using). Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce. If not, add a little more broth.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: French Mustard Chicken with Potatoes and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, golden brown and tender, is presented as the centerpiece on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. It is nestled among tender, 2cm potato chunks and earthy quartered mushrooms, all generously coated in a rich, creamy, light golden mustard sauce. Bright green peas are scattered throughout the dish, providing a vibrant pop of color. A light sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley adds a final touch of green garnish. The plate rests on a simple, dark wood table surface. A folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and warm tones of the dish. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a refined yet casual bistro ambiance, free from distracting elements.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion and cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add quartered mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard until well combined. Add thyme sprigs.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Add potato chunks around the chicken.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pan. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs from the pan. Stir in heavy cream and frozen green peas.
Simmer uncovered for 2-3 minutes, allowing peas to heat through and sauce to slightly thicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Spinach and Three Cheese Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly baked Portobello mushroom is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The mushroom cap is a deep, earthy brown, its edges slightly caramelized from roasting. Nestled within is a generous mound of creamy, golden-brown cheese filling, bubbling gently. Specks of vibrant green spinach are visible throughout the rich, savory mixture. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese creates a delicate crust on top. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping
Offer a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Clean mushrooms. Gently scrape out gills with a spoon. Place cap side down on a baking tray.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté shallot for 3 minutes until softened. Add garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add spinach to pan. Cook until wilted. Remove from heat.
Transfer spinach to a colander. Press firmly to remove all excess water. Chop spinach coarsely.
In a bowl, combine ricotta, cottage cheese, 40g grated Parmesan, breadcrumbs, egg, chopped spinach, shallot, garlic, salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix well.
Spoon filling evenly into each mushroom cap.
Drizzle remaining 10ml olive oil over mushrooms. Sprinkle remaining 10g Parmesan over filling.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Filling should be golden and bubbly. Mushrooms should be tender.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Can be assembled ahead of time and baked just before serving.
Ensure spinach is thoroughly squeezed to prevent a watery filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice is presented in a shallow, wide ceramic bowl. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is nestled prominently on top of a vibrant orange-red bed of short-grain rice. The rice is tender, studded with soft, diced tomato pieces and flecks of minced garlic and onion. The grains are separate yet moist. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and rice, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition is rustic yet refined, showcasing the rich colors and textures of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family style, or in individual wide, shallow bowls.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, shallow pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Stir in diced tomatoes and saffron threads. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing tomatoes slightly, to form a sofrito.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 1-2 minutes to coat rice grains evenly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan loosely or leave uncovered if using a traditional paella pan. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Cover tightly with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Avoid stirring the rice too much once the broth is added to allow the rice to cook evenly and prevent it from becoming sticky.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, allowing the fluid risotto to spread naturally. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm, are visibly integrated, alongside finely diced red bell pepper (1 cm) and sliced brown mushrooms. A vibrant scattering of whole roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst, adorns the surface. Fresh basil leaves, torn, are generously sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of bright green. The colors are rich: golden-brown chicken, deep earthy mushrooms, bright red bell pepper and tomatoes, all against the creamy, pale yellow risotto. The texture is invitingly smooth and tender. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, creating a clean, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.
Heat chicken broth in a saucepan; keep it hot over low heat.

Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.

Finely chop onion and mince garlic. Dice red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 10 ml olive oil and 15 g butter to the same skillet. Add onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the skillet. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladleful (about 250 ml) of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until almost completely absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is al dente (creamy but still firm to the bite), stir in cooked chicken and roasted tomatoes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining 15 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until creamy. Check seasoning; adjust with salt and pepper.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most into the risotto. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with reserved fresh basil.
notes: The key to creamy risotto is to add hot broth gradually and stir constantly.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Risottare (toasting rice and gradually adding liquid)
Mantecare (finishing risotto with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused golden bomba rice forms a slightly mounded base, interspersed with vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and bright green peas. Substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled atop and within the rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The plating is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Cook until wine is almost evaporated.
Stir in the bomba rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Add chicken broth and saffron (steeped in 30 ml warm broth). Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Check seasoning and adjust.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use good quality smoked paprika and authentic saffron threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Rigatoni with Bacon, Mushroom, Artichoke & Sun-Dried Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A generous, well-portioned mound of al dente rigatoni pasta sits centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta is evenly coated in a creamy, off-white sauce, allowing the various ingredients to be clearly visible and well-integrated. Scattered throughout are crispy diced bacon pieces, thinly sliced sautéed earthy brown mushrooms, roughly chopped pale green artichoke hearts, and vibrant, deep red sun-dried tomato strips. A light sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped Italian parsley garnishes the top, adding fresh color and texture. The composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Standard silver flatware is placed beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin lies nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and warm, rustic colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Accompanied by crusty artisan bread for dipping.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Artichoke hearts (canned or jarred, in water or oil)

instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Dice bacon into small pieces. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add bacon and cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside. Keep 15 ml of rendered bacon fat in the skillet.
Thinly slice mushrooms. Add mushrooms to the skillet with bacon fat. Sauté over medium-high heat until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Finely dice shallots and mince garlic. Add olive oil to the skillet if needed. Add shallots and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add white wine to the skillet. Deglaze, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine is reduced by half.
Pour in chicken or vegetable broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Roughly chop artichoke hearts. Thinly slice sun-dried tomatoes. Add artichokes, sun-dried tomatoes, cooked mushrooms, and cooked bacon to the sauce. Stir to combine.
Add cooked rigatoni to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly. Add half of the reserved pasta water, stirring to create a creamy sauce. Add more pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Cook for 1-2 minutes until heated through and sauce clings to the pasta.
Finely chop fresh Italian parsley. Garnish each serving with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash and Sage Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy, free-flowing Roasted Butternut Squash and Sage Risotto is presented on a wide, shallow white porcelain plate. The risotto forms an organic, unforced mound, exhibiting a rich golden-orange hue from the butternut squash, flecked with vibrant green specks of chopped sage and delicate white streaks of melted Parmesan. Tender, slightly caramelized 1.5 cm roasted butternut squash cubes are visibly integrated, with a few additional cubes and whole fresh sage leaves artfully placed on top as a garnish. A light drizzle of high-quality olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft-focus background creating a casual yet refined atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto texture is best enjoyed fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a crisp, dry Italian white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss 600 g butternut squash cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Set aside. Reserve a few roasted squash cubes for garnish.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 320 g Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until the edges of the rice grains become translucent.
Pour in 120 ml white wine. Stir until the wine is completely absorbed by the rice.

Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue this process for 18-20 minutes, or until the rice is al dente and creamy.
During the last 3-5 minutes of cooking, gently stir in most of the roasted butternut squash cubes and chopped fresh sage into the risotto.
Remove the pot from heat. Add 60 g cold, diced butter and 80 g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until the risotto is creamy and emulsified (mantecatura).
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming the risotto with butter and cheese off the heat)

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet and Sour Tofu with Pineapple and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant medley of Sweet and Sour Tofu. Golden-brown, crispy tofu cubes are generously coated in a glossy, amber-hued sauce. Bright red, yellow, and green bell pepper squares, cooked to a tender-crisp texture, intersperse with juicy pineapple chunks. The sauce glistens, reflecting the natural light, coating each ingredient evenly. A sprinkle of fresh, thinly sliced green onions provides a contrasting green pop, alongside a scattering of toasted white sesame seeds for texture and visual interest. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a pair of elegant chopsticks and a small white rice bowl to the side, enhancing the authentic Asian dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed jasmine rice.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks and a small rice bowl.
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2.5 cm cubes.
Cut bell peppers into 2.5 cm squares. Cut pineapple into 2.5 cm chunks.
In a bowl, whisk together vegetable stock, cornstarch, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and tomato paste. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Cook until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove tofu from wok.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add bell pepper squares to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Return tofu to the wok. Add pineapple chunks.
Pour the sweet and sour sauce mixture over the ingredients. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Stir in sesame oil.
Serve hot. Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, and savory flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Beet Puree and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently. Beside it, a vibrant, smooth pool of deep ruby-red roasted beet puree creates a striking color contrast. Glistening strands of sweet caramelized onions are draped delicately over a portion of the chicken. A light drizzle of creamy, pale yellow mustard-mayo sauce artfully trails across the plate, connecting the elements. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green chives, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware is neatly placed beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel beets. Dice beets into 2 cm cubes.
Toss diced beets with 15ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper.
Spread beets on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender.
While beets roast, thinly slice the large onion.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts to hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
While chicken rests, transfer roasted beets and roasted garlic to a food processor. Add red wine vinegar and 60ml chicken stock or water. Blend until smooth puree. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Stir until well combined. Add a teaspoon of water if needed for desired consistency.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of beet puree onto each plate. Place a seared chicken breast next to the puree. Arrange caramelized onions over or beside the chicken. Drizzle with mustard-mayo sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped chives or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Oyakodon presented in a deep, traditional indigo-patterned ceramic donburi bowl. The base consists of a clean mound of steaming, pearlescent Japanese short-grain rice. Draped over the rice is a rich, glossy layer of simmered eggs, featuring a soft and creamy curd texture. Large, succulent chunks of braised chicken thigh are embedded within the egg, showing a light golden-brown exterior. Translucent, thin-sliced onions are interspersed throughout the mixture, coated in a dark umami-rich dashi glaze. The dish is finished with a vibrant garnish of diagonally sliced green scallions and fresh mitsuba leaves. The bowl sits on a minimalist light oak table accompanied by dark wooden chopsticks on a small ceramic rest.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup
Accompany with takuan (pickled daikon radish)
Offer shichimi togarashi (seven-spice powder) on the side
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a wide shallow pan.
Bring the liquid to a simmer over medium heat.
Add sliced onions to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add chicken chunks in a single layer. Simmer for 6 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Slowly pour beaten eggs in a circular motion over the chicken and onions.
Cover the pan immediately. Cook for 45 seconds until eggs are soft-set.
Divide hot rice into four deep ceramic bowls.
Slide a portion of the chicken and egg mixture onto each rice bowl.
Garnish with scallions and fresh mitsuba.
notes: Use a small Oyakodon pan for individual portions if available.
Do not over-beat the eggs to maintain distinct white and yellow streaks.
Ensure rice is hot to help steam the base of the egg mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Jalapeno-Lime Chicken with Creamy Coriander Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown finish, is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken retains its natural shape, showcasing its inviting crust. A vibrant, creamy, pale green sauce is generously spooned over the chicken and pooled around its base, highlighting its smooth texture. A few fresh, bright green coriander leaves are scattered artfully on top of the sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate is set on a simple, warm-toned wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a lime wedge are subtly placed beside the plate. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, emphasizing the rich colors and inviting textures. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, honoring a casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for wrapping
Accompany with a side of Mexican rice or refried beans
Offer extra lime wedges on the side for added zest

ingredients.name: Jalapeno chile
ingredients.quantity: 1-2, deseeded and roughly chopped (adjust to taste)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F).
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven and let rest 5 minutes.
While chicken bakes, prepare the sauce: Combine mayonnaise, chopped fresh coriander, deseeded jalapeno, ground cumin, lime juice, lime zest, and minced garlic in a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
To serve, place one whole chicken breast on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of creamy coriander sauce over and around the chicken.
Garnish with a few fresh coriander leaves or a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust jalapeno quantity to control the spice level. For less heat, remove all seeds and membranes.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek, Black Garlic Tamarind Glaze, Pickled Shallots
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of braised beef cheek rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. The beef, deep mahogany from its rich glaze, is fork-tender, holding its natural, irregular shape. Its surface glistens with dark, viscous black garlic tamarind glaze. Beside the beef, a small, artfully arranged cluster of translucent, ruby-red pickled shallot rings adds a vibrant pop of color and delicate, sharp contrast. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy garlic chips scatter for textural intrigue. A thin, vibrant green cilantro oil line sparingly drizzled, enhancing the dish's sophisticated color palette. Abundant negative space emphasizes minimalist elegance and component perfection. The plate is on a superpremium grey-veined marble, with a folded white linen napkin and modern silver flatware. Dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting luxurious appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: While this is a fine-dining interpretation, traditional Thai meals are often served family-style with rice. For this dish, it is presented as a standalone main course.
instructions: Trim beef cheeks of excess fat. Season heavily with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add sliced ginger, bruised lemongrass, galangal, cilantro roots, white peppercorns, star anise, and cinnamon stick to the pot. Sauté until fragrant.
Return beef to pot. Add beef stock, 20g tamarind paste, 20g palm sugar, and 20ml fish sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cover.
Transfer pot to preheated oven at 150°C. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Return strained liquid to a clean pot. Reduce by half over medium heat.
Thinly slice 100g shallots. Combine rice vinegar, 100ml water, 50g sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Pour over sliced shallots. Let cool.

Thinly slice remaining 100g shallots and all garlic. Heat vegetable oil in a small pan to 140°C. Fry sliced garlic until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Fry sliced shallots until golden and crispy. Remove. Drain on paper towel.

Combine black garlic, remaining 40g tamarind paste, 30g palm sugar, 20ml fish sauce, and 100ml of the reduced braising liquid in a separate pan. Simmer until thickened to a glaze consistency. Blend until smooth.
Blanch a small bunch of cilantro. Immediately shock in ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend with 50ml neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Gently reheat beef cheeks in some braising liquid if needed. Brush generously with black garlic tamarind glaze before serving.
Place one beef cheek per plate. Arrange a small, artful cluster of pickled shallots beside it. Scatter a few crispy garlic chips. Drizzle cilantro oil sparingly around the beef.
notes: Use high-quality beef cheeks for best results. Precision in each component's preparation is key for this minimalist dish.
Ensure the black garlic tamarind glaze is smooth and coats the beef well.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion and Wild Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a minimalist, large white bone china plate with a subtle grey rim, set against a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures. The salad is composed with artistic restraint, featuring a fluid, organic arrangement of rich, dark caramelized red onions intertwined with the varied textures of glossy black and brown wild rice grains. Each element is purposefully placed, leaving abundant negative space on the plate. The deep amber of the onions contrasts with the earthy tones of the rice. A delicate drizzle of golden truffle vinaigrette glistens over the components. A scattering of toasted, pale golden pine nuts provides textural intrigue, while a small, vibrant cluster of bright green pea microgreens is precisely positioned as a fresh, high-contrast accent. The cutting of the onions is thin and uniform, showcasing careful knife work. The wild rice grains are distinct and perfectly cooked. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated simplicity and luxurious refinement, emphasizing the natural beauty of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: microgreens (e.g., pea shoots or radish microgreens)

instructions: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced red onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very tender. Stir in 15 ml balsamic vinegar and a pinch of salt. Cook for 2 more minutes. Set aside.

Rinse wild rice blend under cold water. Combine rice and 600 ml vegetable stock (or water) with a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and grains have burst open. Drain any excess liquid. Fluff with a fork. Let cool slightly.
In a small bowl, whisk together minced shallot, minced garlic, 60 ml extra virgin olive oil, 15 ml white truffle oil, 30 ml balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, gently combine the cooled wild rice and caramelized onions. Add half of the truffle vinaigrette. Toss gently to coat. Taste and adjust seasoning.

On each of four individual fine-dining plates, artfully arrange a portion of the wild rice and caramelized onion mixture. Create an organic, flowing shape. Drizzle remaining truffle vinaigrette sparingly over and around the salad. Scatter a few toasted pine nuts. Place a small cluster of microgreens precisely on top or to the side for visual contrast.
notes: The slow caramelization of the onions is crucial for depth of flavor. Do not rush this step.
The wild rice should be cooked al dente, with some grains burst for textural interest.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Salmon and Zucchini Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve bite-sized Grilled Salmon and Zucchini Bites are artfully arranged on a rustic wooden serving board. Each piece features a tender, pinkish-orange grilled salmon strip, approximately 1.5 cm wide and 6 cm long, snugly rolled within a thin, slightly charred, vibrant green zucchini slice. The zucchini slices exhibit distinct grill marks, adding visual texture. The rolls are presented naturally, some slightly overlapping, creating a casual yet refined arrangement. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh dill and finely grated lemon zest provides a fresh, aromatic garnish, enhancing the natural colors of the dish. The wooden board sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting. The scene is uncluttered, emphasizing the homely comfort and simple elegance of the canapés, suitable for a relaxed family gathering.
instructions: Slice zucchini lengthwise into thin strips, about 3mm thick.
Brush zucchini strips lightly with olive oil. Grill zucchini strips on a preheated grill pan or outdoor grill. Cook until tender with visible grill marks, about 1-2 minutes per side. Set aside.
Cut salmon fillet into strips, approximately 1.5 cm wide and 6 cm long. Season salmon strips with salt, pepper, minced garlic, and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill. Grill salmon strips for 2-3 minutes per side, or until cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F). Do not overcook.
Lay a grilled zucchini strip flat. Place a cooked salmon strip at one end. Carefully roll the zucchini around the salmon. Secure with a small toothpick if needed.
Arrange the rolls on a serving platter.
Garnish with fresh chopped dill or parsley and finely grated lemon zest.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Poblano Chili Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Poblano Chili Bake rests in a rustic, oval ceramic gratin dish. Two large, golden-brown chicken thighs are nestled deeply in a rich, bubbling red-orange tomato and poblano sauce. Strips of softened green poblano peppers are visible throughout the sauce. A generous layer of melted, bubbly Cotija cheese, with golden-brown edges, covers the chicken and sauce. The dish is topped with a sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped cilantro. The texture is hearty and comforting. The gratin dish sits on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a small stack of warm corn tortillas and a dollop of white crema in a small bowl complete the authentic Mexican presentation. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of Mexican rice.
Provide crema or sour cream and lime wedges.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion and poblano strips to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the chicken and sauce.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and cheese is bubbly and golden.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, wide white ceramic bowl, showcasing a single generous portion. Golden-brown, whole chicken thighs are nestled amongst tender, slightly browned potato halves and chunks of soft carrots. A rich, dark, glossy sauce coats the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, clinging to the chicken and potatoes. The chicken skin retains some crispness, contrasting with the tender meat. Vibrant green chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the top, providing a pop of color. The background features a simple wooden table surface with a white linen napkin and minimalist cutlery, illuminated by natural, even lighting for an inviting, refined bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy. About 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Drain most of the fat, leaving about 2 tbsp in the pot. Add sliced onions and carrot chunks. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken and cooked bacon to the pot. Add chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Nestle halved or quartered potatoes around the chicken.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Potatoes should be fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves before serving. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot in shallow bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Salmon Bites with Dill Cream Cheese
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant Seared Salmon Bites are arranged on a simple white ceramic serving platter. Each bite features a thick, golden-brown seared salmon cube, approximately 2.5 cm. This rests on a generous dollop of creamy dill cream cheese, which sits atop a crisp, bright green cucumber round, about 4 cm in diameter. The salmon cubes are uniformly cut and perfectly seared, showing a flaky, pink interior. A small, fresh dill sprig garnishes each bite, adding a vibrant green accent. The presentation is clean and inviting, with natural colors. The platter rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A casually placed cloth napkin creates a homely, relaxed atmosphere. Portions are modest for easy finger-food enjoyment.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry. Remove skin if desired. Cut salmon into 2.5 cm cubes.
Season salmon cubes with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon cubes for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden-brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Set aside.
Finely chop fresh dill.
In a small bowl, combine cream cheese, chopped dill, juice from half a lemon, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth.
Wash cucumber. Slice into 1 cm thick rounds.
Place a small dollop of dill cream cheese mixture onto each cucumber round.
Top each with a seared salmon cube.
Garnish each canapé with a small fresh dill sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan-Style Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Tuscan-style chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh is the focal point, nestled within a rustic, rich red tomato sauce. Surrounding the chicken are vibrantly colored vegetables: large, rustic chunks of roasted potato (3 cm), tender 2 cm squares of red and yellow bell peppers, and softened diced onions. Freshly chopped Roma tomatoes are scattered throughout, adding bright pops of red. The dish is generously topped with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and garnished with a few torn fresh basil leaves. The textures are varied, from the crisp-edged chicken to the tender vegetables and the smooth, glistening sauce. The plate sits on a light wooden table with a white cotton napkin and simple cutlery. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish from the side, with a subtly blurred, warm restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dice onion. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares. Quarter potatoes or cut into 3 cm chunks. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Add potato chunks, ensuring they are partially submerged in the sauce.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Roughly chop fresh Roma tomatoes. Stir them into the sauce during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and torn fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For a deeper flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and remove skin after searing if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Artisanal Sausage Roulade, Egg Noodle Agnolotti with Tofu-Cream Cheese, Broccoli Puree, and Aged Cheddar Foam
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. A vibrant, deep emerald green broccoli puree forms a flowing, organic smear across the lower left quadrant of the plate, creating a dramatic sweep of color. Nestled artfully on the puree are two perfectly seared medallions of golden-brown artisanal sausage roulade, their interiors showing a tightly coiled, finely textured meat. Adjacent to the roulade, three delicate, pale ivory agnolotti are meticulously placed, their soft, inviting curves suggesting a creamy filling. Scattered thoughtfully are a few precisely cut, emerald green beans, lightly charred at their edges, offering a subtle textural contrast and a hint of smoky aroma. A delicate cloud of airy, pale yellow aged cheddar foam rests gracefully on the negative space, adding a sophisticated, ethereal element. The composition is asymmetrical, emphasizing natural forms and abundant white space, drawing the eye to each perfectly executed component. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and the luxurious simplicity of the dish. The surface beneath is a polished grey-veined Carrara marble, subtly reflecting the dramatic, focused overhead lighting, creating soft shadows that enhance depth. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, sits to the side, completing the ultra-minimalist, high-end dining scene.
instructions: Remove casing from sausage. Finely chop shallot and garlic. Sauté shallot and garlic in 10g butter until soft. Cool.
Mix sausage meat with cooled shallot-garlic mixture, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper.
Lay cling film on work surface. Spread sausage mixture evenly into a rectangle, about 1.5 cm thick.
Tightly roll sausage into a cylinder using cling film. Secure ends. Poach in simmering water for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from water. Immediately plunge into ice bath to stop cooking. Chill completely.
Once chilled, unwrap. Sear roulade in hot olive oil until golden brown and crisp on all sides. Rest briefly. Slice into 2 cm thick medallions.
Drain silken tofu well. Combine tofu, cream cheese, a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a food processor. Blend until very smooth. Transfer to a piping bag.
Roll egg noodle dough thinly. Pipe small mounds of filling onto one half of the pasta sheet, spaced evenly.
Fold other half of pasta over filling. Press around filling to seal, removing air. Cut into small agnolotti shapes using a pasta wheel or knife. Ensure edges are well-sealed.
Cook agnolotti in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente. Drain gently.
Trim broccoli into florets. Blanch in salted boiling water until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to preserve color.

Drain well. Blend blanched broccoli with 20g butter, a splash of hot water (if needed for consistency), salt, and pepper until perfectly smooth. Pass through a fine sieve for extra silkiness. Keep warm.
Trim green beans. Blanch in salted boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Transfer to ice bath. Drain.
Heat a dry cast-iron pan or griddle until very hot. Char green beans briefly until slightly blistered and tender-crisp. Season with salt.
Grate aged cheddar. Heat chicken stock and milk in a saucepan. Add grated cheddar. Stir until cheese melts.
Season with salt and pepper. If desired, add a tiny pinch of xanthan gum for stability. Transfer mixture to a siphon bottle. Charge with N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie.
On each plate, create a sweeping smear of vibrant broccoli puree.
Arrange 2-3 slices of seared sausage roulade artfully on the puree.
Place 3-4 agnolotti delicately around the roulade.
Add a few charred green beans for contrast and texture.
Dispense a cloud of aged cheddar foam beside the main elements.
Garnish with a microgreen or a single small herb sprig for a pop of color and freshness.
notes: Ensure sausage is cooked to 75°C internal temperature.
For the foam, use a good quality aged cheddar for distinct flavor.
The key to this dish is precision in cutting, cooking, and plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef & Orzo Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve golden-brown Spicy Beef & Orzo Croquettes are artfully arranged on an elegant white rectangular porcelain serving platter. Each croquette is a perfect oval, approximately 5 cm long, with a visibly crisp, textured breadcrumb coating. The deep-fried exterior boasts a rich golden-amber hue. A few finely chopped fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the croquettes for a pop of vibrant green. The croquettes are spaced evenly, allowing each piece to stand out. In the background, a simple wooden table surface provides a warm, natural base. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the croquettes' appetizing crust. A small white ramekin filled with a vibrant red spicy tomato dipping sauce is positioned to the side, inviting interaction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of simple marinara sauce or a spicy arrabbiata sauce for dipping.
Arrange on a large platter for communal sharing, typical of Italian antipasti.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add minced beef. Brown beef, breaking it up with a spoon. Drain any excess fat. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Stir in chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Cook orzo pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine cooled beef filling, cooked orzo, and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Mix thoroughly.

Take about 30g of the mixture. Flatten slightly in your palm. Place a small cube of mozzarella in the center. Carefully shape the mixture around the mozzarella into an oval or cylindrical croquette, about 5 cm long. Repeat for all mixture.

Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs. Dredge each croquette in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Roll in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat enough olive oil for deep-frying in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crisp. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure beef filling is completely cooled before mixing with orzo and forming croquettes. This helps them hold shape.
Do not overcrowd the frying pot to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.
For an extra kick, a pinch of red pepper flakes can be added to the beef filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Tomato & Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken thigh, golden-brown and whole, sits prominently. Beside it, or partially underneath, is a rustic mound of vibrant roasted cherry tomatoes, some burst open, mixed with tender, caramelized red onion wedges. The rich red and deep brown hues of the sauce create a striking contrast with the chicken. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the dish, adding a pop of color. Delicate, thin shavings of pale yellow Parmesan cheese are generously draped over the chicken and tomato mixture. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard, elegant flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the delicious pan sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes and red onion wedges with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tomatoes burst and onions caramelize.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Add roasted tomatoes and onions to the skillet. Stir to combine with the broth and garlic. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to warm through and meld flavors.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet with the tomato and onion mixture. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Transfer chicken and sauce to a white porcelain dinner plate. Garnish generously with fresh torn basil leaves and shaved Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Squash and Peanut Dip with Brown Rice Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting starter portion of creamy, golden-orange roasted squash and peanut dip is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The dip forms a casual mound, topped with visible specks of finely chopped fresh green parsley for vibrant contrast. Alongside, a cluster of irregular, golden-brown brown rice crisps are artfully placed, showcasing varied textures. The presentation is homely and comforting. The plate rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden kitchen table, showing subtle signs of use. A simple, folded linen napkin is casually placed nearby. Soft, warm lighting, reminiscent of a cozy family kitchen, highlights the food's natural colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread squash on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Squash should be tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool slightly.
Rinse brown rice. Combine with 250ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 35-40 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let cool.

Spread cooked brown rice thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Bake at 180°C for 20-30 minutes, or until crispy. Break into irregular pieces.
In a food processor, combine roasted squash, peanuts, coconut butter, minced garlic, lemon juice, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Process until smooth. Add water gradually, 15ml at a time, until desired creamy consistency is reached.
Transfer dip to a serving bowl. Chop parsley finely. Garnish dip with chopped parsley. Serve with brown rice crisps.

recipes.recipe_name: Almond Chia Seed Energy Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Almond Chia Seed Energy Bites are arranged casually on a small, rustic ceramic plate. Each bite is a roughly spherical shape, about 3-4 cm in diameter, with a natural, slightly irregular surface. Their color is a warm, light golden-brown, flecked with tiny dark specks from the chia seeds. The texture appears soft and slightly dense. The bites are placed organically on the plate, some touching, creating a relaxed, unpretentious cluster. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded linen napkin is placed nearby. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting, homemade quality of the snack. Portions are generous, inviting casual sharing.
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine almond flour, chia seeds, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Add peanut butter, maple syrup, and vanilla extract to the bowl.
Mix all ingredients until a firm, cohesive dough forms. Use hands if necessary.
Roll dough into small, uniform balls, approximately 20-25g each. This yields about 10-12 bites.
Place the formed bites on a plate or tray lined with parchment paper.
Chill in the refrigerator for a minimum of 30 minutes to firm up before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Simmered Chicken and Daikon
recipes.special_requests: Japanese cuisine, Low calories, high protein
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Japanese Simmered Chicken and Daikon is presented in a traditional ceramic donburi bowl. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. The chicken is cut into rustic 4 cm chunks, showing its tender, simmered texture with a light golden-brown hue from the broth. The daikon pieces, cut into 2 cm thick quartered rounds, are translucent and soft, nestled amongst the chicken. Both ingredients are immersed in a glossy, amber-colored dashi-based broth. A scattering of bright green, thinly sliced green onions provides a fresh contrast on top. The arrangement is natural and comforting, with components slightly overlapping. Beside the bowl, a pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick holder. A small, humble tea cup and a tiny dish of light green tsukemono (pickles) complete the homely setting. The lighting is warm and soft, mimicking natural kitchen light, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal. The plate is adequately filled without being overcrowded, showcasing a wholesome, home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a bowl of freshly steamed white rice.
Accompany with a small side of miso soup.
Offer a variety of tsukemono (Japanese pickles) on the side.
Eat using chopsticks.
instructions: Trim excess fat from chicken thighs. Cut chicken into 4 cm chunks.
Peel daikon radish. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds. Quarter each round.
Optional: Place daikon in a pot. Cover with water. Boil for 5 minutes. Drain water.
In a large pot, combine dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Stir to dissolve sugar. Add thinly sliced ginger.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add blanched daikon and chicken chunks to the simmering liquid.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 20-25 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Daikon should be tender.
Remove from heat. Let the dish rest, covered, for 5 minutes for flavors to deepen.
Thinly slice green onions for garnish.
Ladle simmered chicken and daikon into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh green onions.
notes: For a richer flavor, use boneless, skin-on chicken thighs and remove skin after cooking to keep it low calorie.
Adjust the amount of sugar to your preference for sweetness.
Pre-boiling the daikon helps remove any slight bitterness and allows it to absorb flavors better.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Glazed Chicken Thighs with Roasted Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Glazed Chicken Thighs is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate. A plump, golden-brown chicken thigh, glistening with a vibrant reddish-orange glaze, is placed centrally. The glaze is thick and clings to the chicken, showing hints of the savory sear beneath. Beside the chicken, several tender, deeply roasted red onion wedges with slightly caramelized edges are artfully arranged. Their purple and brown hues contrast with the chicken. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut red onions into 1.5 cm thick wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, 2 g salt, and 1 g black pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with remaining 3 g salt and 1 g black pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.

While chicken sears, combine hot sauce, honey, minced garlic, soy sauce, and apple cider vinegar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and stir in butter until melted and smooth.
Pour half of the prepared glaze over the seared chicken thighs in the skillet. Turn to coat the chicken.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Brush chicken with remaining glaze. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Slice chicken thighs into thick medallions or serve whole. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Serve immediately with a side of rice or a fresh green salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Worcestershire Beef Bites with Crispy Shallots
